newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $0.50- trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $0.50- trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower Thursday, pressured by sluggish demand for pork, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota were seen ranging from $57.00 to $57.50.
Illinois top prices at the plant could range $56.50 to $57.00 and Indiana/Ohio top plant prices for hogs could range $56.00 to $56.50, sources there said.
Prices on some pork cuts were quoted lower at midday -- a scenario likely to erode packer operating margins.
The lower prices also spurred talk that weekend slaughter would be light, sources said.

Fresh loin prices at midday were not well tested, USDA said, while skinned hams were weak to $1.00 per cwt lower and bellies were $1.00 to $3.00 lower. There were 29.5 pork loads and 15.5 loads of pork trimmings sold.
Slower pork demand was attributed to ideas that retailers had booked enough orders to get them through the Christmas holiday and would only be in the market for spot, fill-in type business.
